note.backdrop: Monday's session closed far lower than it opened: the S&P 500 -1.92% to 7,416, the Nasdaq Composite -2.49%, the Dow -1.41%, the 10-year yield up 0.05 point to 5.15% (Motley Fool wrap); QQQ -2.67%, SPY -1.91%, IWM -1.66% (StockTitan). The VIX closed 18.7% higher (the bank's close). After the close the market is flat: SPY +0.0%, QQQ +0.1%, IWM -0.2%, VIX +0.0%. The check flagged a market-wide move from S&P futures -1.9% and oil -4.0%, but both lines are measured from Friday: the futures' and oil's Monday daily bars are held back while their sessions are open, the flaw found last week. On the 5-minute charts, futures were 7,439.5 at Monday's 4pm close and 7,435.25 at 11:20pm ET (-0.06%), and oil $85.47 against $85.01 (-0.5%); bitcoin has moved -0.2% since the close. So the flag is the check's artifact, not a move. One stock is outside its 9-in-10 range after the close: Red Cat, on results.

read.says: Monday: Nasdaq Composite -2.49% to 24,510, S&P 500 -1.92% to 7,416, Dow -1.41%, 10-year 5.15%; Nvidia -4.12%, Intel -7.02%, Dell -6.96%, AMD -5.58% on new export restrictions on advanced AI chips to Southeast Asia; a Fed governor's warning on corporate debt weighs on debt-financed AI build-outs; Tyson +8.72% on results; Nvidia reports Tuesday, Anthropic prices its offering Wednesday night and trades Thursday.
At Monday's close QQQ -2.67%, SPY -1.91%, DIA -1.43%, IWM -1.66%; CG Oncology +13.95% at the close on its bladder cancer trial; Red Cat sank after hours.

Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim rule on Monday requiring licenses to export, re-export or transfer advanced AI chips to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, to stop restricted countries reaching US chips by renting computing in third-country data centers.

A Fed governor said last week there is a risk of a large correction in stocks if AI investment does not pay off, citing more than $800 billion of AI capital spending in 2026, much of it financed with corporate bonds, and what looks like circular financing among AI companies.

The Senate's defense bill carries three chip measures (congressional review of AI chip licenses, chip tracking abroad, allied limits on chipmaking tools); no vote has been taken; Nvidia's $108 billion third-quarter guidance excludes China data-center sales.

The House Speaker said on Nov 12 there is a developing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China; Nvidia billed $7.9 billion to customers in China including Hong Kong in the quarter to July 26, 8.2% of its total.
Icahn Enterprises closed at $3.60 on Monday, down 15.09%, after its units went ex-distribution for the $0.50 distribution to holders of record on Nov 16.

Red Cat withdrew its full-year 2026 revenue target: funding and contract awards have come more slowly than expected and the outcome of the Drone Dominance program's Gauntlet II removed an expected contributor; third-quarter revenue $11.8 million (+22%), nine months $47.4 million; cash $242.7 million.
S&P 500 futures on the 5-minute chart: 7,439.5 at Monday's 4pm ET close, 7,435.25 at 11:20pm ET.
Oil futures on the 5-minute chart: $85.47 at Monday's 4pm ET close, $85.01 at 11:20pm ET.

singles.beneath: It was worth about $540 million at the close, with $242.7 million of cash and nine months' revenue of $47.4 million: the price leaned on the target. It also proposes to buy Steyr Motors. The drone stocks it moved with over the year (Unusual Machines, Ondas, Kratos) barely moved after the close.

Third-quarter revenue was $11.8 million (+22% on the year); Zacks puts it 70% below estimates.

themes.beneath: Nvidia's own direct China exposure is small: its $108 billion third-quarter guidance already excludes China data-center sales, and China including Hong Kong was $7.9 billion, 8.2% of revenue, in the quarter to July 26 (Yahoo; MLQ). The rule's reach through Southeast Asian data centers is the part no one has sized. Nvidia reports on Tuesday after the close, under an interim chief; Anthropic prices its offering on Wednesday night. The desk's open calls (made on Nov 13, due Nov 20) put Nvidia's move by Friday at 7.5% or more with chance 0.50, AMD's at 9% or more at 0.42, Dell's at 9.5% or more at 0.40; they are sizes, either way.
themes.cause: The selling deepened through the session and closed near its lows. From the bank's closes: Nvidia -4.1%, AMD -5.6%, Intel -7.0%, Micron -7.6%, Sandisk -8.6%, Lam -6.7%, Teradyne -7.1%, Dell -7.0%, Super Micro -6.8%, IREN -9.8%, Applied Digital -8.7%, Ciena -8.2%, Lumentum -8.5%, Bloom -7.7%; among the buyers Oracle -5.0%, Alphabet -4.1%, Amazon -3.3%, Meta -2.4%, Microsoft -1.1%, Apple -1.0%. Two things were reported on the day. Commerce issued an interim rule requiring licenses for advanced AI chips sent to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, to stop restricted countries renting computing in data centers there (CBS); the Motley Fool wrap ties AMD's fall to it. And a Fed governor's warning from last week was back in the news: a large correction is possible if AI spending does not pay off, with over $800 billion of it in 2026, much financed with bonds; the wrap ties Dell's fall to warnings about debt.
themes.mechanism: The rule reaches the chip sellers through the data centers of those five countries, a fast-growing market for US chips; how much of their sales go there is not reported in what I read. Congress's bills (review of chip licenses, tracking chips abroad) remain unvoted (Yahoo, Nov 10), but the Speaker spoke of a developing consensus on Nov 12 (MLQ). The debt warning reaches the buyers that borrow to build (Oracle and Alphabet fell most of them) and everyone they buy from. My inference: the market is marking down how much AI hardware gets bought and on what money, not one company's trouble. Microsoft and Apple fell least; that this is because they borrow less to build is my guess, not something I read.
themes.name: The AI markdown closed at its worst, with a new chip-export rule and a warning about AI debt
themes.watch: Nvidia's results and outlook on Tuesday evening, and what it says about Southeast Asia. The rule's text in the Federal Register (one report gives operators 90 days; not confirmed). Whether Microsoft and Apple keep falling less than the other buyers.

That it also drags the small treasuries is my inference, untested.
